newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi shares end short-trading week higher.
newsitem.headline: Saudi shares end short-trading week higher.

text.p: Saudi shares ended the week slightly higher in moderate trade focused on services sector shares, figures from the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) showed on Saturday.
The index ended 0.72 percent higher at 162.63 points from 161.47 points on April 13th, before Eid al-Adha Moslem holiday which ended on Monday.
Of the 54 companies traded, 31 rose, 11 declined and 12 were unchanged.
Services sector shares accounted for 37 percent of trading volume, which BFA put at 2.14 million shares worth 481 million riyals.
Makkah Co was the star perfomer of the week ending 11.7 percent higher at 296 riyals from a previous 265 riyals.
Among other gainers was Saudi Cable which closed at 118 riyals from 111 riyals, Al-Bank Al-Saudi Al-Faransi which closed at 253 riyals from 244 riyals.
Saudi Pharmaceutical Industries and Medical Apliances Corporation (SPIMACO) ended the week 8.1 percent lower at 194 riyals from 211 riyals.
